t.E459.agn: In 2016 EFSA saw no need to change the existing acceptable daily intake (ADI) of 5 mg/kg body weight; however, it reported that in the brand-loyal consumption scenario, which it considered the most realistic, this limit was exceeded at average consumption in all age groups except infants, and at high consumption in all groups. JECFA had also set an ADI of 0-5 mg/kg body weight in 1995.
t.E459.body: Beta-cyclodextrin is poorly absorbed when ingested by animals and humans; in the large intestine it is broken down into maltose and glucose by gut bacteria and amylase enzymes.
t.E459.eff.0.t: The daily limit may be exceeded with brand-loyal consumption
t.E459.eff.0.w: All age groups except infants (average consumption), all groups (high consumption)
t.E459.eval: A ring-shaped sugar obtained from starch; it encapsulates flavourings and vitamins. In its 2016 re-evaluation EFSA maintained the ADI (5 mg/kg body weight per day), but reported that in the brand-loyal consumption scenario this value was exceeded at average consumption in all age groups except infants, and at high consumption in all groups.
t.E459.found.1: Food supplements in tablet and coated tablet form
t.E459.prod: It is produced from starch by enzymatic conversion.
t.E459.regx.0: Re-evaluated; ADI of 5 mg/kg body weight per day maintained, ADI exceedance reported in the brand-loyal scenario.
t.E459.regx.1: ADI of 0-5 mg/kg body weight per day.
t.E459.summary: A ring-shaped sugar molecule produced from starch with enzymes. It holds flavourings and vitamins and makes them stable.
t.E459.what: It is a ring-shaped sugar obtained from starch that protects flavourings, additives and vitamins by enclosing (encapsulating) them.
